S&P now forecasts capex above $225bn in 2027 (from $163bn) and free operating cash flow deficits of $22bn in 2026 and $71bn in 2027, with debt rising above its downgrade threshold by 2028. Apple overtakes Nvidia to become world's most valuable company amid tech selloff

stories.summary: Yahoo Finance says Alphabet lost about $766bn of market value in October and nearly 13% in the week, its worst week since August 2011, mostly after Thursday's results. It said a close at or below $280.50 would make October its worst month in percentage terms since its 2004 listing; the shares closed Friday at $279.84. Its price-to-earnings ratio is now at its lowest in more than a decade.

stories.summary: Investing.com puts Meta's October fall at 15.2% and Alphabet's at 18.6%, as worries about AI spending and negative free cash flow hit big tech. Yahoo Finance says Amazon lost about $70bn of market value in the week after its results. UBS's Ulrike Hoffmann-Burchardi told investors to build portfolios with exposure beyond tech, while still seeing scope for share gains overall.

sources.title: Alphabet's October wipeout hits $766 billion, its worst month ever

stories.summary: Yahoo Finance says Alphabet had the second-largest weekly loss of value for any US-listed stock, about $477bn at Friday's low, and that SpaceX, Intel and Nvidia each lost more than $100bn. Software names including ServiceNow and Fortinet fell roughly 25-33% over the week. Eli Lilly, Tesla and SK Hynix added about $370bn between them.

explainer.meaning: A monthly survey of purchasing managers; a reading above 50 means activity is growing and below 50 means it is shrinking.

stories.headline: China's factories shrink again in October: official PMI 49.3, down from 50.1

sources.title: China's manufacturing PMI softens, high-tech sector maintains expansion
China Manufacturing PMI Falls to 49.3 in October as Export and Domestic Demand Soften

stories.summary: China's official manufacturing PMI fell 0.8 points to 49.3 in October, back below the 50 line that separates growth from contraction, Xinhua reports. The high-tech manufacturing PMI stayed in expansion at 51.3. Other reports call it the third contraction in four months, with export and home demand softening.

explainer.meaning: The extra amount added to a price because traders fear supply could be disrupted, rather than because of actual shortages.

stories.headline: Brent hits about $117 as tankers are hit near the Strait of Hormuz; oil set for a fourth monthly rise

sources.title: Oil prices set for sharp monthly rise on Hormuz strikes and US threat to hit Iran

stories.summary: Brent rose 2.4% to about $117.56 and WTI to $104.17 on Friday afternoon, putting Brent on course for a gain of about 15% in October, The National reports. Iran's Revolutionary Guard said a tanker hit a mine on an unauthorised route, and another was damaged by explosives attached by a small boat. Trump said the war will be wrapped up soon, having earlier said the US would not strike Iran before the 3 November midterms.

topline: No trading since Friday's close: the Nasdaq sits about 7.8% below its 6 Oct high and VWRP closed at £140.68, 4.4% off its high.
S&P put Meta's credit rating on negative outlook, forecasting a $71bn free-cash-flow deficit in 2027 from AI spending; Meta lost 15.2% in October.
Alphabet's October fall of nearly 19% was its worst month since listing; Apple overtook Nvidia as the most valuable company after Nvidia's 4.2% drop on Friday.
Gold fell 7.2% in October to near a one-year low; Iran reported more tankers halted by mines in the Strait of Hormuz, with Brent above $117.
Coming up: Grab and Fabrinet results Monday after the US close; US midterms Tuesday, Bank of England Thursday, Vistra results and US jobs Friday.
